# Void interface default forwarding

A package final child of a named static parent forwards its original receiver to
an explicit default on the second direct interface. The original no-argument
void method has no result register. Only its owned bridge access bit is encoded;
every original compiler Code byte and other declaration remains unchanged.

Frozen callers, reflection, method handles and rebuilt callers observe receiver
identity, wide state updates, reentry, callback order, partial effects and exact
throwables. Source and external-provider layouts compile every emitted unit and
check all original declarations and Code roles. Independent wrong programs and
javac superclass controls qualify the observer before recovery.
